MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETINGS
  MONDAY, AUGUST 4, 2025

1.  CALL TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by CHAIR OLSON at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

CHAIR OLSON led those assembled in the Pledge of Allegiance.

3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Olson, Nicklas,  Medawar,  Repp-Loadsman,  Romanelli,
  Schachter, Yoo

  City Staff Present:  Jeannie Naughton, Community Development Director
  Cameron Hall, Assistant Planner
  Carol Corea, Administrative Analyst

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

A.  APPROVAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, JUNE 2, 2025

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSIONER MEETING MINUTES OF JUNE 2, 2025.

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

NONE

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL SUCH
  ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6A

There being no objection, CHAIR OLSON so ordered.

B.  BIANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT – JANUARY 1, 2025 TO JUNE 30, 2025

CHAIR OLSON congratulated Assistant Planner Hall on his promotion.

CHAIR OLSON stated that there are cases on the report that have been open for several years and
asked about putting a procedure in place to bring these into compliance. He also asked if the number
of cases related to work without permits is a normal percentage for the size of the city and asked if
there is a way to provide more education to residents on the type of work that requires permits.
CHAIR OLSON stated that from personal experience and comments from residents in his
neighborhood, the permit process is still slow and cumbersome. He stated that it may be worth
looking into whether the transition to Willdan has been a good move for the city.

There were no further comments. The report was received and filed.

  1
Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2025
 7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250177; ADDRESS: 4559 Marloma Drive, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Ashley and Matt Tullius; A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination (NC-250180) and approval of a Grading application (G-250181)
  for the construction of retaining walls, swimming pool, and outdoor fireplace/kitchen area that
  would require the excavation of earth materials greater than three feet in vertical height and
  the importation of 117 cubic yards of earth materials.

Assistant Planner Hall provided a presentation summarizing the staff report for Planning Application
No. PA-250177. The project proposes to regrade the sloped rear yard along with drainage
improvements; construct a new 120 foot long, 5 foot high retaining wall along the eastern property
line and below the existing deck. The new retaining wall will help to stabilize the area below the patio.
The project also proposes a new 400 SF 12 SF high trellis with associated hardscape and BBQ and
a 400 SF gravel firepit area, and a 20 foot X 40 foot pool with associated pool decking in the northwest
corner of the lot. Assistant Planner Hall stated that the proposed project meets the criteria for
Neighborhood Compatibility.

Staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve Planning Application No. PA-250177,
subject to the conditions outlined in the staff report.

CHAIR OLSON inquired about a chain link fence beyond the north corner property line. Assistant
Planner Hall stated that it is in the easement and noted that the proposed retaining wall will be
installed at the property line. Director Naughton stated that there are many fences and improvements
in the City’s right-of-way that staff have discussed internally. Many of these would warrant a more
comprehensive approach if the City began requiring lease agreements and encroachment permits.
At this time existing improvements can remain, however, when a property owner proposes
improvements to their property, the city would ask that they obtain an encroachment permit and
potentially a lease agreement.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN asked if there is a reason to not require that the fence be
relocated. Director Naughton stated that there is not, however, there has been discussion at policy
development sessions with City Council and internally with staff and the direction is that existing
improvements remain, until the City establishes a comprehensive approach. COMMISSIONER
MEDAWAR added that many properties throughout the city are not flat and in some cases, property
owners need to encroach onto city property to install fencing to secure their properties.

CHAIR OLSON inquired if there is concern with a prescriptive easement. Director Naughton stated
that she will need to defer this question to the City Attorney. COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN
stated that in her past experience with Palos Verdes Estates, there would not be a prescriptive
easement, and as soon as the City requires the relocation of unapproved assets, then it is cleared
for public use.

CHAIR OLSON asked that a condition of approval be added, that the property owner understand that
the fence is on city property and they may be asked to remove it at any time.

There was no objection by the planning commissioners or staff.

CHAIR OLSON stated that he did not see a drainage plan included and asked if it will be required.
He stated that during heavy rain mud runs down onto Palos Verdes Drive North. Director Naughton
stated that the project will be subject to low impact development requirements. She stated that this
can be added as a condition of approval.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR NICKLAS to,

  APPROVE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250177 WITH THE CONDITIONS OUTLINE
  IN THE STAFF REPORT AND THE ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS REGARDING THE
  ACKNOWLEDGEMENT THAT THE CITY MAY AT ANY TIME REQUEST THAT THE FENCE
  IN THE PUBLIC RIGHT-OF-WAY BE REMOVED; AND THAT A DRAINAGE PLAN IS
  REQUIRED.

AYES: Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
August 4, 2025
 8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250112; ADDRESS: 22 Sorrel Lane, Rolling Hills
  Estates, CA 90274; APPLICANT: Ryan Carstensen, Charles E. Thomas, Inc.; A request for
  a Neighborhood Compatibility Determination (NC-250113) for first-and second-story additions
  to an existing one-story residence, a Variance (V-250114) to allow construction within non-
  conforming east and west side yard setbacks, a Variance (V-250115) for legalizing an existing
  non-conforming front yard setback, a Grading Application (G-250234) for import of more than
  20 cubic yards of earth materials and fill that is more than three feet in height at its deepest
  point and two Minor Deviations for (MD-250244) an encroachment into a required front yard
  that does not project beyond the forwardmost building line and (MD-250245) a decrease of
  less than 10% of the required front yard.

Director Naughton stated that a neighbor of the subject property came into the city late today and
expressed concern about the project, including view impacts, neighborhood compatibility, trees and
soil erosion. Staff has not had an opportunity to visit the neighbor’s property in order to see the view
impacts and is requesting that this item be continued to the September 8 Planning Commission
meeting to provide sufficient time to visit the property and perform an analysis of whether the view
impacts would change the recommendation.

COMMISSIONER REPP-LOADSMAN made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR
to,

  CONTINUE PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-250112 TO THE SEPTEMBER 8
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING.

AYES: Olson, Nicklas, Medawar, Repp-Loadsman, Romanelli, Schachter, Yoo
NOES:
ABSENT:
ABSTAIN:

9.  COMMISSIONER ITEMS

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR requested an update about Silver Saddle. Director Naughton stated
that this is an active code enforcement case and staff is actively working on this with the property
owners.

COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR requested an update on 758 Silver Spur Road (Bart Earle Way).
Director Naughton stated that this is also a code enforcement case. CHAIR OLSON asked if the
Planning Commission approval expired. Director Naughton stated that the applicant has made
changes to the project and the project will need to come back to the Planning Commission for
approval.

COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated that the Planning Commission and the City Council had a joint
meeting to discuss several items. The discussion was continued to a future joint meeting and he
inquired if a date has been determined. Director Naughton stated that a date has not been determined
at this time, but it will be sometime in the fall or winter of this year.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

Director Naughton stated that due to Labor Day this meeting should be adjourned to the Planning
Commission meeting scheduled on September 8, 2025.
